stem: A nurse is using USPSTF recommendations when counseling an asymptomatic client about preventive screening. Which approach is most accurate?

options.A: Apply the specific recommendation only to clients who match its defined population, age/risk criteria, and clinical context.
options.B: Apply every USPSTF recommendation to every person regardless of age or risk.
options.C: Treat a USPSTF recommendation as a diagnosis of disease.
options.D: Ignore the population description because screening recommendations never depend on risk or age.

rationale: USPSTF preventive-service recommendations define the population to which each recommendation applies. Screening decisions should therefore be based on the exact recommendation's population and risk criteria rather than generalized to everyone.
educational_objective: Apply preventive screening recommendations to the population for whom they were developed.
source_locator: Recommendation tables — each preventive service specifies population and recommendation
source_claim_supported: USPSTF screening recommendations apply to defined populations and clinical/risk contexts rather than universally to every client.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9/PDF p.13
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive screening
correction_summary: Removed broad generic wording and made population/risk matching the exact screening principle tested.
